newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shoppers warm to first day of winter sales.
newsitem.headline: German shoppers warm to first day of winter sales.

text.p: Germany's much-bemoaned consumption downturn was little in evidence on Monday as bargain-hunters stormed the high streets on the first day of the country's nationwide winter sales.

Despite chilly weather conditions, shoppers thronged the stores to snap up items reduced by as much as 70 percent and retailers were already predicting better till receipts from this year's sale than were seen last year.
Branded high-fashion items and sports gear were the biggest first-day sellers in the sales which run through February 8, rather than cheaper mass-produced items.

"Impulse buys are getting increasingly rare," said a spokeswoman for Kaufhaus des Westens (KaDeWe) in Berlin, Germany's largest and newly renovated department store, which is expecting 20 percent higher turnover this winter.

In Munich, long queues formed outside the doors at the Kaufhof department store, while Hertie's branch in Dresden, which was selling skirts and trousers for five to 10 marks ($3-$6), had sold out of snowsuits and girls' dresses by lunchtime.

However the German retailers' association HDE was less sanguine. Stores were placing their hopes on the winter sales, said HDE managing director Thomas Werz, but the overall outlook remained bleak because of slow wage rises in recent years.

Meanwhile a consumer climate index produced by Germany's ICON consulting firm on Monday revealed a slight one point advance to 88 in December, showing that pessimists continue to well outweigh optimists on German consumption trends.
"Germans are expecting a slight improvement in economic developments. But this tiny hint of optimism is not yet enough to cause a fundamental change in behaviour," ICON said.
